 Motor racing-Sao Paulo qualifying delayed as heavy rain hits Interlagos
 Sunday, 08 Nov 2026
 | 3:39 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Formula One F1 - Sao Paulo Grand Prix - Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, Sao Paulo, Brazil - November 7, 2026 Fans wear rain ponchos in the grandstand as qualifying is delayed due to heavy rain REUTERS/Jean Carniel 
 SAO PAULO, Nov ⁠7 (Reuters) - Qualifying for Formula One's ⁠Sao Paulo Grand Prix was delayed on ‌Saturday after heavy rain swept across Interlagos, the latest weather disruption at a circuit renowned for ​dramatic wet races and ⁠qualifying sessions.
 Rain began ⁠falling shortly after the end of the third ⁠and ‌final practice session and intensified in the minutes before qualifying ⁠was due to start at 3 ​p.m. local ‌time. Drivers initially left the pitlane ⁠as scheduled, ​but a red flag was brought out two minutes later as conditions deteriorated.
 As soon ⁠as he joined the ​track, newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli told his Mercedes team over the radio that ⁠he was "already aquaplaning". Safety car driver Bernd Maylander carried out assessments of the circuit.
 "It's very simple to say it's ​not drivable, it's too ⁠dangerous," Maylander told Sky TV. "A lot of ​standing water, even on ‌the straights, that creates high-speed ​aquaplaning."
 (Reporting by Gabriel Araujo and Alan Baldwin, editing by Ed Osmond)
